new_findings.kind: positive_determination_gap (a text-showing operator a viewer executes is never recorded: inline-image end differs from viewers)
new_findings.file_line: src/content.rs:87-102 (EI accepted only with white space BEFORE it, :96, and a non-regular byte after, :97); src/sanitized_save.rs:644-646 (an unfiltered inline image is skipped: no check of its length against /W /H /BPC /CS); src/redaction.rs:842-854 (the selector sees only the image's unit square)
new_findings.evidence: pdf.js parser.js:202-336 (findDefaultInlineStreamEnd) ends unfiltered inline-image data at 'E','I' followed by SPACE/LF/CR whose next bytes lex to a known operator, with NO white-space requirement before E (state machine :215-224; :331-335 'data is immediately followed by the EI marker (fixes issue10388.pdf)'); MuPDF pdf-interpret.c:837-856 likewise scans for 'E','I' + delimiter after the image decoder, no white space required before E. Content 'q 1 0 0 1 500 50 cm BI /W 1 /H 1 /BPC 8 /CS /G ID AEI Q BT /F1 12 Tf 100 700 Td (SECRET-ALPHA) Tj ET EI' (F1 Helvetica): both viewers read image data 'A', then Q and BT..ET (SECRET-ALPHA drawn at 100,700), then ignore the stray EI. content.rs rejects 'AEI' (no white space before) and ends the image at the later ' EI', so 'Q BT .. Tj ET' is image data: the Walker records no ShowRec for it, the selector never sees it, page_classes has nothing to mark, inline_images() skips it as unfiltered. Region [90 690 200 715]: nothing selected, residual pass (same parser) 0, no needle, every RECORDED operator determined: region_cleared() and is_proven() true while SECRET-ALPHA is drawn in the region. With a /Differences or Identity-H font the hidden run also escapes every byte spelling of a removed needle. The decision's invariant ('EVERY text-showing operator ... in EVERY content stream') is broken by the parser, not by the walk.
new_findings.remediation: Fail closed on inline-image extent: compute the exact data length of an unfiltered image from /W /H /BPC /CS (/IM, /D) and the end-of-data of an implemented filter, and read the stream as content_unreadable (NotProven::UnreadableContent; selector refusal) whenever any other 'E','I' + white-space candidate a viewer could accept exists (before or after the computed end) or the lengths disagree; regression test with the pdf.js no-leading-space case and an independent oracle (the text is still in the saved bytes).

new_findings.kind: R9-F1 class (writing mode read horizontal while viewers write vertically)
new_findings.file_line: src/determination.rs:121-128 (only `def` with exactly the two operands [/WMode v] sets a mode), :74-82 (no mode found = Horizontal), :99-130 (an embedded CMap's /CMapName is never read)
new_findings.evidence: (a) pdf.js cmap.js:552-557 + :573-575 and MuPDF pdf-cmap-parse.c:94-104 + :398-399 set the mode from ANY integer token that follows the name /WMode, whatever operator comes next (non-zero = vertical). An embedded CMap program '/CMapName /X def /WMode 1 1 begincodespacerange <0000> <FFFF> endcodespacerange 1 begincidrange <0000> <FFFF> 0 endcidrange endcmap' (also '/WMode 1 pop', '/A /WMode 1 def', '[/WMode 1] def', '<< /WMode 1 >> def') is vertical in both viewers; determination.rs sees begincodespacerange/def with other operand shapes, records no mode, combine([]) = Horizontal. (b) pdf.js cmap.js:344-357 + :683-690 replaces an embedded CMap named /Identity-V with a full identity map (exactly the r9_cmap fixture body with '/CMapName /Identity-V def' and no /WMode) by the built-in vertical Identity-V; determination.rs reads Horizontal. With r9_cmap_doc and R9_BELOW either reads region_cleared() and is_proven() true (no VerticalText mark, no UnresolvedWritingMode) while the run is drawn down through the region: the outcome writing_mode_is_read_from_the_cmap guards only for '/WMode 1 def'. V4-06 verdicts determination.rs:98/:123 ('never assumed horizontal') are therefore false.
new_findings.remediation: Read the program as viewers do: every /WMode name followed by an integer sets the mode (non-zero vertical), /WMode followed by anything else is Unresolved, a /CMapName that is a vertical Table 116 name (Identity-V, V, ...-V) is vertical; or fail closed: any program containing the name /WMode in another shape than '/WMode 0 def' is Unresolved. Add the spellings to writing_mode_is_read_from_the_cmap.

new_findings.kind: PLR-039 / R9-F2 class (/Subtype read without resolving a reference: the selector and the page walk skip a form a viewer draws; a Type 0 font reads as simple)
new_findings.file_line: src/redaction.rs:564 and :586 (xobject(): d.get("Subtype").is_some_and(|s| s.is_name(..)) on the raw value; an indirect /Subtype returns None and the Do is ignored, no mark); src/show_text.rs:678 (walker skips the Do), :924-926 (content_role_streams form/image tests); src/encoding.rs:83 (is_composite); contrast show_text.rs:946 and encoding.rs:111 which do resolve
new_findings.evidence: ISO 32000 7.3.10 lets any object be indirect; pdf.js Dict.get dereferences (primitives.js:108-125) and paintXObject reads xobj.dict.get("Subtype") (evaluator.js:1820-1825). (a) Form '<< /Type /XObject /Subtype 30 0 R /BBox [0 0 612 792] /Resources << /Font << /F1 6 0 R >> >> >>' (object 30 = /Form), content 'BT /F1 12 Tf 100 700 Td (SECRET-ALPHA) Tj ET', page 'q /Fm1 Do Q', region [90 690 200 715]: xobject() returns None (no FormXObject/Image mark, nothing removed), the walker does not enter it from the page (not in draws, so not in page_classes), content_role_streams walks it as Stray with its own Helvetica (determined, horizontal), no needle, residual 0: region_cleared() and is_proven() true while a viewer draws SECRET-ALPHA in the region. An image XObject with an indirect /Subtype in the region is never marked Image either. (b) A Type 0 font '/Subtype 31 0 R' (31 = /Type0) /Encoding /Identity-V with a /ToUnicode that names every byte: is_composite false, so walker and selector read it as a simple horizontal font (FontState::Known, no VerticalText), while viewers draw it vertically.
new_findings.remediation: Resolve /Subtype (and /PatternType, /Type) through res()/doc.resolve() at every site (grep get("Subtype")) or treat a non-name value as unresolved (fail closed); add indirect-/Subtype form, image and Type 0 cases to a region test.

new_findings.kind: determined_but_wrong reading (composite-font codes split by the /ToUnicode map, not by the font's /Encoding CMap)
new_findings.file_line: src/show_text.rs:590-594 and src/redaction.rs:403-410 (composite text read with Cmap::decode_checked), src/cmap.rs:229 (lens = the ToUnicode map's own codespace lengths), :250-266 (shortest length with a mapping wins)
new_findings.evidence: Viewers split a Type 0 string into codes by the font's /Encoding CMap and look each code up in /ToUnicode by numeric value (pdf.js fonts.js:3660 cMap.readCharCode, :3566 toUnicode.get(charcode); Identity-H = 2-byte codes, cmap.js:645-650). Identity-H font, string <015301450143015201450154012D0141014C015001480141>, /ToUnicode with codespaces <00>-<FF> and <0000>-<FFFF>, 2-byte bfchars <0153>->S <0145>->E ... and 1-byte bfchars <01>->Q <53>->Z <45>->Z ... plus <7E>->S <7D>->E ... (so Cmap::encode picks 1-byte codes): pdf.js extracts SECRET-ALPHA (and the font program draws those CIDs); the walker reads 'QZQZ...' with complete = true, so the operator is positively determined (Known, Horizontal, readable), no reading carries the needle, the code-spelling backstop spells 7E 7D .. and the UTF-16 hex spelling is 0053 ..: neither occurs. An appearance or stray copy of a removed SECRET-ALPHA reads is_proven() true; the selector's removed_unicode uses the same split.
new_findings.remediation: Split composite strings with the /Encoding CMap's codespace (Identity-H/V: 2 bytes; embedded CMap: its begincodespacerange; a predefined CMap whose codespace the crate does not hold: unreadable) and look /ToUnicode up by code value; or mark the operator unreadable when the ToUnicode code lengths differ from the Encoding codespace. Regression test: Identity-H font with a mixed 1-/2-byte ToUnicode.

new_findings.kind: operand-position differential (crate takes the FIRST operand, viewers the LAST)
new_findings.file_line: src/redaction.rs:758 (Tj/' string = operands.get(0)), :777 (TJ array = first), :713 (Tf name = first), :857 (Do name = first); src/show_text.rs:644 (Tf), :651 (gs), :668 (Do) use operands.first()
new_findings.evidence: pdf.js evaluator.js:5449-5455 shifts extra LEADING operands off a fixed-arity operator (Tj, TJ, Tf, Do numArgs per :5308-5316) and executes it with the last ones; MuPDF keeps only the last string/name token (pdf-interpret.c:1669-1674; Tj :1430-1434). (a) 'BT /F1 12 Tf 100 700 Td (A) (SECRET-ALPHA) Tj ET', region [120 690 180 715]: the selector boxes '(A)' (100..108), keeps the operator; viewers draw SECRET-ALPHA across 100..192; the walker records both strings as determined text; nothing removed, residual 0: region_cleared() and is_proven() true. (b) '/Fm0 /Fm1 Do' on the page: crate enters Fm0, viewers draw Fm1 (with own /Resources Fm1 is only walked as Stray, never seen by the selector) -> same outcome as R10-F3. (c) '/F9 /F1 12 Tf' in an appearance: the walker reads the codes through /F9 (determined) while viewers use /F1 (e.g. a /Differences font that draws SECRET-ALPHA): plain verify_payload_absent misses it (the selector errors Malformed on the same Tf, so a redaction fails closed there).
new_findings.remediation: Fail closed: an operator with more operands than its arity (or a Tj/TJ/Do/Tf/gs with operands of the wrong type) makes the stream content_unreadable and the selector refuse; or use the last N operands exactly like viewers in both walker and selector.

new_findings.kind: geometry claimed known but not computed (decision (c)); DESCRIPTOR/doc overclaim (V4-07)
new_findings.file_line: src/redaction.rs:451-469 (show(): composite fonts 1000 per BYTE, /W and /DW never read; Tc added per byte; Tw only for simple fonts; vertical box ts - 0.25|fs| .. ts + 0.95|fs| whatever the sign of fs); src/show_text.rs:287-301 (ShowRec::geometry reports nothing for horizontal non-Type3 fonts); docs src/redaction.rs:9-13 and DESCRIPTOR redaction.geometry ('upper bound for standard fonts', 'box -0.25..+0.95 em', 'Over-removal is safe; under-removal is not')
new_findings.evidence: (a) Composite width: pdf.js evaluator.js:4145-4147 reads /DW (default 1000) and /W; spacing is per glyph (canvas.js:2918). Identity-H font with /DW 3000 and a full ToUnicode, '100 700 Td <0001...000A> Tj' at 12 pt: viewer origins 100, 136, ..., 424; the selector box is 20 bytes x 12 = [100, 340]; region [350 690 450 715] holds glyphs 8-10 and is not touched: region_cleared() true (no mark: Known, Horizontal). (b) Negative font size: pdf.js canvas.js:2512-2519 + :2810-2816 draws Tf < 0 rotated 180 degrees (ISO 9.4.4 Trm = [Tfs*Th 0 0 Tfs 0 Trise] x Tm x CTM); 'BT /F1 -12 Tf 100 700 Td (SECRET-ALPHA) Tj ET' (Helvetica /Widths) draws caps from y about 691.4 to 700, x 8..100; the box is y [697, 711.4]; region [20 689 90 696] is not touched while the lower part of every glyph is drawn inside it. (c) 'upper bound for the standard fonts' is false: Helvetica and Helvetica-Oblique '@' 1015, Symbol arrowboth/arrowdblboth 1042, ZapfDingbats 1016 (pdfminer.six fontmetrics); the -0.25..+0.95 em box is below Symbol's FontBBox (-293..1010) and Helvetica-Bold's ascent (962); with Tc < 0 the last glyph's ink lies |Tc| beyond the advance box. No test proves any of these bounds.
new_findings.remediation: Either mark as RegionIncomplete (new RedactionClass or reuse UnresolvedFont-like class) every text whose geometry the selector does not compute exactly: composite fonts until /W /DW and per-code Tc/Tw are read, fs < 0 (or use the signed Tfs in the vertical box), simple fonts without /Widths that are not standard-14 with known metrics; or compute it (/W, /DW, per-code spacing, signed size, FontBBox-based vertical extent, ink beyond the advance). Correct redaction.rs:9-13 and DESCRIPTOR redaction.geometry, citing the tests that prove the bound (V4-07).

new_findings.kind: normalised matching skipped for printable-ASCII streams (decision (3) names XMP; doc claim false)
new_findings.file_line: src/sanitized_save.rs:532-538 (stream_text_hits returns nothing when every byte is printable ASCII: 'anything else is covered by the byte spellings'), needles normalised only for text matching at :826-832, byte spellings from the unnormalised needle text :331-347
new_findings.evidence: A removed string drawn with a ligature or punctuation glyph has a needle text that differs from its normalised form: '(con\200dential plan)' in a Type 1 font with /Differences [128 /fi] is read 'con\uFB01dential plan' (AGL fi = U+FB01; reading_of keeps it, redaction.rs:415). Its spellings are the raw bytes, PDFDoc 'con\x93dential plan', UTF-8 'con\xEF\xAC\x81dential plan', UTF-16 and hex: none matches an uncompressed or Flate XMP packet '<dc:description>confidential plan</dc:description>' (pure ASCII). stream_text_hits would match the NFKD-normalised needle 'confidential plan' but returns early because the stream is printable ASCII; the same title as an /Info string IS found (strings are always normalised, :842-853). Result: is_proven() true while XMP keeps the removed words. Same for needles holding NBSP or white-space runs ('SECRET\u00A0ALPHA' vs ASCII 'SECRET ALPHA'). Pre-existing before R9 (no normalised stream matching existed), but the R9 design and decision (3) now claim XMP is matched after normalisation.
new_findings.remediation: Run stream_text_hits on every non-exempt, non-raster stream (or skip only when every NORMALISED needle is printable ASCII and equal to its byte spelling); add an ASCII-XMP case with a ligature needle to zero_width_and_compatibility_characters_never_hide_text.

new_findings.kind: normalisation gap (decision: zero-width characters removed): Default_Ignorable_Code_Point subset
new_findings.file_line: src/norm.rs:40-58 (is_ignorable); DESCRIPTOR proof.normalisation lists the same ranges; V4-06 verdicts norm.rs:42/:99 say 'default-ignorable characters'
new_findings.evidence: Unicode DI (ICU4X icu_properties_data 2.3.0): U+00AD, U+034F, U+061C, U+115F-1160, U+17B4-17B5, U+180B-180F, U+200B-200F, U+202A-202E, U+2060-206F, U+3164, U+FE00-FE0F, U+FEFF, U+FFA0, U+FFF0-FFF8, U+1BCA0-1BCA3, U+1D173-1D17A, U+E0000-E0FFF. new_findings.kind: normalisation gap: bidi overrides reorder what a viewer shows
new_findings.file_line: src/norm.rs:47-51 and :99-101 (U+202A-202E and U+2066-2069 dropped, their reordering ignored); doc claim norm.rs:3-4 ('found whatever invisible ... characters it is spelled with')
new_findings.evidence: UAX #9: characters between RLO (U+202E) and PDF (U+202C) are displayed right to left. Outline title (UTF-16BE) '\u202EAHPLA-TERCES\u202C plan' is shown in a bookmark panel as 'SECRET-ALPHA plan'; normalise() drops the controls and keeps 'AHPLA-TERCES plan': no hit for SECRET-ALPHA, is_proven() true. Not in the lead decision's normalisation list (escapes, zero-width, NFKC); the module claim is broader than the code.
new_findings.remediation: Treat any text string or reading that contains an explicit directional override/embedding/isolate as unreadable for the proof (fail closed) or also match the visually reordered form (UAX #9 L2 for the override runs); weaken norm.rs:3-4 otherwise.

new_findings.kind: decision deviation (disclosed): NFKC only for Latin targets
new_findings.file_line: src/norm.rs:14-21, src/norm_data.rs (2008 code points); DESCRIPTOR proof.not_covered 'compatibility characters whose decomposition leaves Latin text'; lane residuals_for_lead item 3
new_findings.evidence: Decision: 'Unicode NFKC'. Needles outside Latin are not NFKC-matched: halfwidth katakana (U+FF65-FF9F), Greek mathematical letters (U+1D6A8..), Arabic presentation forms, Kangxi radicals, CJK compatibility ideographs and canonical equivalents outside U+0300-036F (Greek tonos precomposed U+03AC vs alpha + U+0301; Hangul syllables vs conjoining jamo). A Japanese or Greek removed string reappearing in such a form reads as proven. Disclosed, so V4-07 is met; whether this satisfies 'NFKC' is the lead's call.
new_findings.remediation: Lead decision: accept the Latin-only scope as recorded, or generate the full NFKD table (or require an NFKC-normalisation crate decision).

new_findings.kind: suppression path: whole-token exemption judged on the reading, not on the drawing
new_findings.file_line: src/sanitized_save.rs:500-506 (exempt when a letter of the same string touches the match), :374-382 (byte token rule)
new_findings.evidence: Appearance 'BT /F1 12 Tf -598 5 Td (xSECRET-ALPHA) Tj ET' with a Helvetica dict whose /Widths gives code x (120) the advance 50000: the x is drawn at -596 (outside the BBox, clipped) and SECRET-ALPHA from about 4 pt on, visibly alone. The reading 'xSECRET-ALPHA' lies in one string glued to 'x', so the match is exempt; the raw spelling fails the byte token rule: verify_payload_absent reads clean. The decision allows exemption only 'when the drawn reading proves a different token'; a glued letter placed far away (hostile /Widths) or drawn by a blank glyph proves nothing.
new_findings.remediation: Exempt only when the glued letter is drawn adjacent (selector-style advance check within the string) or not at all in drawn text (exemption only for string objects); or record the limit in DESCRIPTOR proof.not_covered.

new_findings.kind: decoding_disagreement (DIFF class: a code read by a rule narrower than what a viewer draws) on the removal side
new_findings.file_line: src/redaction.rs:413-418 (reading_of keeps the encoding reading only when same_words says the letters or digits differ; otherwise the needle is the byte text), src/encoding.rs:185-189 (same_words ignores punctuation, spaces and quote shapes)
new_findings.evidence: When a /Differences encoding changes only punctuation, spaces or quotes, the viewer draws different text than the bytes but removed_unicode is None, so the needle is the BYTE text. Typical pdfTeX T1/OT1 fonts: code 0x27 = /quoteright, 0x7B = /endash (OT1). Region text '(Smith's account)' is drawn 'Smith\u2019s account' (reading 'Smith\u2019s account', same_words true -> needle 'Smith's account'); an outline twin written by hyperref as UTF-16 'Smith\u2019s account' normalises to itself (NFKC keeps U+2019) and does not match 'Smith's account': is_proven() true while the bookmark shows the removed words. Same for '1990{1995' drawn '1990\u20131995', and for a Differences [32 /hyphen] remap. The walker's hay uses the encoding reading (show_text.rs:600-605), so the miss is only on the needle side. Pre-existing (carried verdict redaction.rs:415 from 49731a5:389), not raised before.
new_findings.remediation: Use the complete encoding reading as needle text whenever it differs from the bytes at all (not only in letters/digits), keeping the byte text as a second needle; regression test with /Differences [39 /quoteright] and a UTF-16 outline twin.
